failures.description: A template catalogue entry named chat was presented as a strong AI chat runtime feature.
failures.expected: Catalogue JSON may be described as metadata but must not establish a runtime feature.
failures.actual: AI chat was reported as a strong feature with two symbols.
failures.root_cause: Feature source signals accepted non-executable JSON catalogue content as runtime behavior evidence.
failures.regression_test: tests/V3FeatureEvidenceTest.php — catalogue JSON named chat cannot create AI chat

failures.description: A completed partial scan was stored as a crash after Windows returned -1 from proc_close.
failures.expected: Use the final proc_get_status exit code and preserve the partial scan result.
failures.actual: The corpus record said failed with an empty crash reason.
failures.root_cause: Alpha child-process orchestration discarded the final non-negative exit code on Windows.
failures.regression_test: tests/AlphaRunnerTest.php — successful child exit codes survive delayed Windows process polling

failures.description: Quick analysis exhausted 128 MiB while decoding unbounded TypeScript worker evidence.
failures.expected: Bound worker output, disclose partial evidence, and finish below the memory ceiling.
failures.actual: PHP exhausted memory in NodeWorkerAnalyzerProvider while decoding the worker graph.
failures.root_cause: Node workers emitted unbounded symbol and relationship arrays while PHP retained duplicate input buffers.
failures.regression_test: tests/V3AstTest.php — semantic output is capped before PHP graph decoding

failures.description: Self-dogfood attempted an authentication-gated remote despite an explicitly authorized local repository being available.
failures.expected: Use a static exact-commit detached clone from the authorized local repository.
failures.actual: Safe Git import failed because terminal authentication was disabled.
failures.root_cause: The initial corpus importer only supported anonymous public HTTPS repositories.
failures.regression_test: tests/AlphaRunnerTest.php plus WTFCode exact-commit corpus rerun

failures.description: Documentation and reference URLs inside executable files were reported as runtime external services.
failures.expected: Require endpoint configuration or network-call evidence at the exact source line.
failures.actual: Dozens of documentation sites, placeholders, and malformed hosts appeared as services.
failures.root_cause: Language adapters promoted every URL-shaped string in a runtime-path file without checking line-level execution context.
failures.regression_test: tests/V3FalsePositiveTest.php — comments and website strings do not prove services while API_BASE_URL does

failures.description: Flask was confidently identified as FastAPI because both frameworks support app.get decorators.
failures.expected: Framework identity requires framework-specific import, manifest, or package-path evidence.
failures.actual: The Flask repository stack was FastAPI.
failures.root_cause: A generic Python route decorator was accepted as FastAPI identity evidence.
failures.regression_test: tests/UnitTest.php — generic decorators do not prove FastAPI and explicit Flask evidence does

failures.description: Generic migration plan and service-worker register symbols became Billing and user Registration features.
failures.expected: Feature terms must distinguish product behavior from unrelated technical meanings.
failures.actual: Django showed Billing and a CRUD client showed Registration with strong confidence.
failures.root_cause: Standalone plan and register terms were semantically ambiguous despite multi-signal scoring.
failures.regression_test: tests/V3FeatureEvidenceTest.php — migration plans and service-worker registration stay outside product features

failures.description: Alpha run summaries retained feature labels but omitted the evidence needed for manual truth review.
failures.expected: Store bounded feature paths, lines, signal classes, and confidence without storing source content.
failures.actual: Reviewers had to rerun or grep repositories to understand feature claims.
failures.root_cause: The harness summarized feature counts too aggressively.
failures.regression_test: tests/AlphaRunnerTest.php — every feature summary carries bounded evidence metadata

failures.description: A native detector change reused a pre-change provider cache entry because only the aggregate analysis version changed.
failures.expected: Every native extraction behavior change invalidates native provider cache keys.
failures.actual: The Flask route regression saw a stale graph with zero routes after the adapter was added.
failures.root_cause: AnalysisEngine::NATIVE_VERSION remained unchanged across native detector behavior changes.
failures.regression_test: tests/UnitTest.php plus provider-version cache invalidation coverage

failures.description: Repeated identity and source-text matches promoted framework internals to strong product features without graph or route corroboration.
failures.expected: Strong feature confidence requires an independent graph or route signal; ambiguous technical terms do not establish features.
failures.actual: Flask internals appeared as strong Login and Registration features.
failures.root_cause: Cluster confidence counted repeated symbols as corroboration and feature vocabulary included generic session, register, query, and email terms.
failures.regression_test: tests/V3FeatureEvidenceTest.php plus original Flask corpus rerun

failures.description: Resume validity ignored the Alpha run schema, so old summaries could be reused after evidence fields changed.
failures.expected: Repository SHA, analyzer version, profile, and harness schema must all match before resume skips work.
failures.actual: Alpha.3 runs created before feature evidence was added qualified for reuse.
failures.root_cause: Resume identity omitted ALPHA_SCHEMA_VERSION.
failures.regression_test: tests/AlphaRunnerTest.php — run schema version is part of the resumable contract

failures.description: A documentation/specification repository showed strong product features sourced from e2e specs and asset-generator tooling.
failures.expected: Specification suites and generators remain visible as files but cannot establish runtime product behavior.
failures.actual: Profile, Login, and Search appeared as strong features on a non-application repository.
failures.root_cause: RuntimeEvidencePolicy excluded tests and generated output but omitted specs and generator directories.
failures.regression_test: tests/V3FeatureEvidenceTest.php plus original RealWorld index rerun

failures.description: An optional transitive AWS package in a lockfile was reported as an actively used runtime service.
failures.expected: Dependency manifests and lockfiles may inform package inventory but cannot prove runtime service use without executable import, client, endpoint, or deployment evidence.
failures.actual: AWS appeared beside Postgres although the application contained no AWS runtime source.
failures.root_cause: Service enrichment treated a lockfile line containing both client and aws-sdk as executable runtime context.
failures.regression_test: tests/V3FalsePositiveTest.php — manifest and lockfile package presence cannot prove AWS runtime use

failures.description: SQL-like prose outside runtime source created a database table named the.
failures.expected: Database operations require executable source or a runtime-path SQL file; prose and support material cannot define application tables.
failures.actual: The literal word after FROM in prose appeared as a table in application summaries.
failures.root_cause: Product database enrichment ran before the shared runtime-evidence boundary.
failures.regression_test: tests/V3FalsePositiveTest.php — SQL-like README prose cannot create a database table

failures.description: Release scripts and a load generator contributed strong runtime feature evidence.
failures.expected: Support scripts and load generators stay inspectable but cannot establish end-user product behavior.
failures.actual: A release helper supported Search evidence and a load-test client supported Checkout evidence.
failures.root_cause: The shared runtime-path policy did not classify scripts and load generators as support material.
failures.regression_test: tests/V3FeatureEvidenceTest.php — release scripts and load generators cannot create product features

failures.description: Configuration comments, plugin metadata URLs, and Stripe's apiVersion property were presented as AWS, github.com, and Kubernetes runtime services.
failures.expected: A service requires a runtime client/import/call, a strongly named literal endpoint, or matching deployment configuration.
failures.actual: Three unrelated strings appeared as active service boundaries.
failures.root_cause: Endpoint matching accepted comments and generic URL metadata, while a colon in apiVersion made it look like a protocol marker.
failures.regression_test: tests/V3FalsePositiveTest.php — comments, metadata URLs, and generic API version fields cannot prove services

failures.description: Alpha route samples retained the source file path but omitted the detected URL route and framework.
failures.expected: Manual reviewers can compare the actual route path, source file, framework, line, and confidence.
failures.actual: Four distinct React Router entries all looked like GET src/App.js in the summary.
failures.root_cause: The bounded Alpha serializer selected path but omitted route_path and framework from the fused route contract.
failures.regression_test: tests/AlphaRunnerTest.php — schema 3 invalidates summaries that omit route evidence

failures.description: A direct Can I delete this file question returned a generic symbol trace without a deletion-safety conclusion.
failures.expected: Distinguish confirmed use, possible convention/configuration use, and no detected use without claiming deletion is safe.
failures.actual: The answer counted related evidence but left the user to infer whether deletion was safe.
failures.root_cause: Deterministic explanations had feature and file search paths but no conservative deletion-specific wording.
failures.regression_test: tests/V3ExplanationTest.php — confirmed dependents and no-detected-use answers both refuse unsafe deletion claims

failures.description: A deletion question naming the full chat route path answered about an auth route with the same basename.
failures.expected: An exact repository path always wins over a basename fallback.
failures.actual: Can I delete app/(chat)/api/chat/route.ts selected app/(auth)/api/auth/[...nextauth]/route.ts.
failures.root_cause: Deletion assessment returned the first basename match before checking all candidates for an exact path.
failures.regression_test: tests/V3ExplanationTest.php — duplicate route filenames resolve the explicitly named repository path

failures.description: A repository with explicit Express dependency and imports was described only as a generic Node API.
failures.expected: Retain the useful generic server category while naming the statically proven Express framework.
failures.actual: The stack and architecture summary omitted Express.
failures.root_cause: The Express branch intentionally collapsed framework identity into the generic Node API label.
failures.regression_test: tests/Benchmark.php --id=express-realworld — public benchmark requires Express and Node API

failures.description: The architecture found authentication but the stack omitted the directly declared Auth.js framework.
failures.expected: A direct next-auth or @auth/core dependency identifies Auth.js without requiring name heuristics.
failures.actual: The stack named Next.js, Drizzle, Database, and Vercel but not Auth.js.
failures.root_cause: Framework stack classification had no Auth.js dependency rule.
failures.regression_test: tests/V3FalsePositiveTest.php — direct next-auth dependency identifies Auth.js while a generic next key still does not prove Next.js

failures.description: The repository-level summary centers one Flask service and does not reconstruct the polyglot Go/gRPC microservice topology.
failures.expected: A monorepo overview ranks service boundaries and cross-service contracts above a minority framework.
failures.actual: The overview says Flask application, Database, and Docker with one route.
failures.root_cause: Architecture synthesis is repository-global and has no normalized gRPC/service-boundary model for polyglot monorepos.
failures.regression_test: tests/alpha/scorecards/microservices-demo.md — manual accepted-limitation review

failures.description: The scanner maps client routes but does not summarize the application's CRUD behavior or its remote tutorial API flow.
failures.expected: A useful trace connects Add/Edit/Delete UI actions to the shared HTTP client without inventing a backend implementation.
failures.actual: React and four routes are correct, but the feature catalogue is empty and service understanding is weak.
failures.root_cause: Feature vocabulary and transport enrichment do not combine generic CRUD components with the shared client across files.
failures.regression_test: tests/alpha/scorecards/react-crud.md — manual accepted-limitation review

failures.description: Feature traces find correct entry symbols but frequently hit the hop presentation cap without surfacing terminal tables or services.
failures.expected: A bounded trace prioritizes UI to handler to API to data/service endpoints and clearly names missing hops.
failures.actual: Correct checkout/chat/upload starts coexist with up to 80 mixed library/UI hops and empty terminal collections.
failures.root_cause: Breadth-first trace traversal and relevance ordering do not reserve budget for terminal effects.
failures.regression_test: tests/alpha/scorecards/supabase-payments.md and vercel-ai-chatbot.md — manual hop review

failures.description: The bounded large-framework scan completes at roughly 126 MiB under a 128 MiB worker ceiling.
failures.expected: Large partial scans retain a safer memory margin while disclosing file and graph limits.
failures.actual: The run is correctly partial and no longer crashes, but operates very near the ceiling.
failures.root_cause: Three thousand analyzed Python files plus fused provider graphs retain substantial in-process evidence.
failures.regression_test: tests/alpha/reports/performance.md — near-ceiling outlier remains visible

failures.description: The first project screen rendered 12 identical Database operation cards from one file.
failures.expected: The first screen prioritizes distinct risk categories while detailed stored findings remain available elsewhere.
failures.actual: Repeated operations pushed other useful information below the fold.
failures.root_cause: The overview queried findings by severity without collapsing repeated type and title combinations.
failures.regression_test: tests/UnitTest.php — first-screen findings collapse duplicate signatures

failures.description: A TypeScript Select import from radix-ui was displayed as a database table named radix.
failures.expected: SQL SELECT FROM detection cannot consume JavaScript/TypeScript module import or export syntax.
failures.actual: The Understand screen listed radix beside real migration tables.
failures.root_cause: The case-insensitive single-line SQL pattern matched Select as ... from before language syntax was excluded.
failures.regression_test: tests/V3FalsePositiveTest.php — Select imports cannot create SQL tables

failures.description: The feature-trace page overflowed horizontally at a 390 px mobile viewport.
failures.expected: Panels, hop rows, and code evidence remain within the viewport while long evidence is ellipsized.
failures.actual: The document was 562 px wide in a 390 px viewport.
failures.root_cause: Single-column grid tracks and hop content retained automatic minimum widths from long code/import evidence.
failures.regression_test: Playwright 390x844 trace acceptance — document scroll width equals viewport width

failures.description: A focused detector fix was labeled as potential scope drift because its implementation file fell into the generic Application code area.
failures.expected: Generic application-code edits that implement a specifically described data, auth, API, or UI change do not create scope drift by themselves.
failures.actual: The comparison treated Application code as an unexpected area even though tests were the only other changed area.
failures.root_cause: Scope comparison exempted tests but did not account for Application code being the generic container for specific implementation areas.
failures.regression_test: tests/V3ChangeTest.php — generic application code remains aligned with specific change intent

failures.description: The stated intent Add semantic AST dependencies did not map the plural word dependencies to the configuration/dependency area.
failures.expected: Both dependency and dependencies classify the intended change as configuration and dependency work.
failures.actual: The intent fell back to Application code and made the expected dependency-file changes look like potential scope drift.
failures.root_cause: The intent matcher recognized dependency but not its plural dependencies form.
failures.regression_test: tests/V3ChangeTest.php — plural dependency intent maps to configuration and dependencies

failures.description: Persisted route samples named SHA-256 route identities handler_key, causing 250 generic API-key findings in the Git-scoped secret gate.
failures.expected: Human-review artifacts retain route evidence without unnecessary secret-shaped internal identifiers.
failures.actual: The values were non-secret hashes, but their field name and entropy created high-volume secret-scan noise.
failures.root_cause: The bounded artifact copied an internal graph identity that was not needed for manual route review.
failures.regression_test: tests/AlphaRunnerTest.php — route samples omit internal handler_key values
